title: Are veneers permanent? What cannot be undone, what wears out, and what happens next
seoTitle: Are Veneers Permanent? Reversibility, Lifespan, Removal
description: Veneers are not reversible, but they are not forever either: what 0.3 mm of enamel means, replacement after 10 to 15 years, removal, and the 5-year warranty.
author: Dr. Gretell Alonso Fiel, DMD
imageAlt: A plaster dental model with porcelain veneers on its front teeth beside a small brass hourglass on cream linen, in soft morning light
answer: Veneers are **not reversible**: a thin layer of enamel, about 0.3 mm at Xiluet Smiles, is prepared before bonding, and enamel does not grow back. They are **not forever** either. Porcelain veneers last 10 to 15 years or more, and then they are replaced, not removed. The tooth underneath stays yours, protected by the veneer, and every veneer we place carries a 5-year written warranty.

sections.h2: Two questions hiding inside one word

blocks.p: When people ask whether veneers are permanent, they usually mean one of two things. **Can I undo this?** And **will it last the rest of my life?** The answers point in opposite directions, which is why so much of what you read online sounds contradictory. Veneers cannot be undone, because a little enamel is prepared to make room for them. And they do not last a lifetime, because porcelain, like anything in a mouth, wears and eventually gets replaced.

Both the [American Dental Association](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/veneers) and the [Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/23522-dental-veneers) say the same thing in plain words: the treatment is not reversible because enamel is removed, and a veneer typically lasts 10 to 15 years with good care. So the honest answer is a commitment to a restored tooth, not a commitment to a particular piece of porcelain. Once you see it that way, the rest of the decision gets easier.

sections.h2: Why veneers are not reversible, even at 0.3 mm

blocks.p: Enamel is the only tissue in your body that cannot repair itself. It has no living cells, so, as the [Cleveland Clinic puts it](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/24798-tooth-enamel), once it is gone it does not grow back. Any preparation, however small, is therefore a one-way step. Front-tooth enamel is about 1 mm thick; our veneers are about 0.3 mm, so the preparation stays in the outer third and the nerve, 2 to 3 mm further in, is never approached. But the surface that was smoothed is smoothed for good.

Some teeth need no preparation at all. Small, short or set-back teeth gain exactly the thickness of the veneer, which is why the [porcelain veneers page](/porcelain-veneers-miami) says "0.3 mm, sometimes none". Even then, calling the result reversible is a stretch: a bonded veneer comes off with a drill and polishing, not with a snap, and the bonding resin has to be cleaned from the enamel. [Minimal prep versus no-prep](/blog/minimal-prep-veneers-vs-no-prep-veneers) goes into when each applies. The accurate phrase for both is enamel-preserving, not reversible.

blocks.quote: I tell patients the truth in one sentence: you are not choosing a veneer for 15 years, you are choosing to have a restored tooth for life. If that sentence sits comfortably, you are ready.

sections.h2: What is permanent, and what is replaceable

blocks.p: It helps to separate the parts. The prepared surface is for life. The veneer is a component with a long but finite service life. The bond between them is renewed every time a veneer is replaced. Your digital design file is kept, so a replacement can match the shape you approved rather than starting from scratch.

blocks.p: The lifespan numbers are better than most people expect. Pooled data on more than 6,500 veneers found [95.5% still in place at 10 years](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7961608/), and a 20-year study found 91%. When a veneer does fail it is usually a chip or a veneer coming loose, most often in the first two years. [How long porcelain veneers last](/blog/how-long-do-porcelain-veneers-last) goes through the data in detail, so this article will not repeat it. The point here is simpler: a veneer that reaches the end of its life is replaced, and the tooth under it continues.

sections.h2: What happens if a veneer is removed

blocks.p: Veneers are removed for three reasons: they have worn out, they were poorly made somewhere else, or a tooth under one needs treatment. Removal is routine. The dentist cuts through the porcelain with a fine bur, lifts it off and polishes the remaining resin from the enamel. The area is numbed for comfort. What is left is the tooth you had, very slightly matte where it was prepared. [What teeth look like under veneers](/blog/what-do-teeth-look-like-under-veneers) has photos of exactly this moment.

What you cannot do is leave the tooth that way. A prepared surface is more sensitive to cold, picks up stain faster and, after years under a veneer, no longer matches its neighbors in shape or color. In practice a removed veneer is replaced the same week, usually the same visit, with a new veneer, or, if a previous dentist removed far more enamel, with a crown. At Xiluet Smiles, removing an old smile design made elsewhere is $500, and [fixing veneers gone wrong](/blog/how-to-fix-veneers-gone-wrong) explains how we assess what the earlier work left behind.

list: **Worn or chipped after 10 to 15 years:** replaced with a new 0.3 mm veneer, often from your original design.
**Bulky, opaque or badly fitting work from another clinic:** removed, the margins cleaned, and a new veneer made in our lab.
**Decay or a crack under the veneer:** treated first, then a veneer or a crown depending on how much tooth remains.
**You simply want them gone:** possible, but the tooth will still need a thin veneer or bonding to look and feel normal.

sections.h2: How minimal preparation changes the answer

blocks.p: The amount of enamel removed on day one decides what your options are in year fifteen. A veneer prepared to 0.3 mm leaves roughly 0.7 mm of enamel. When that veneer is replaced, the new one bonds to enamel again, and the one after that can too. A veneer prepared to 0.7 mm or more, which is common with thicker conventional porcelain, often reaches dentin. Dentin bonds less reliably, and each replacement tends to take a little more tooth, so the second or third restoration on that tooth is more likely to be a crown.

The data agrees. In a 15-year study of 672 veneers, those bonded mostly to enamel survived at [96.7% versus 93.9%](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jerd.70016) when more dentin was exposed. So the question to ask any clinic is not "are your veneers permanent" but "how much enamel will you remove, and will my next dentist still have enamel to work with." The aggressive preparations behind the ["do veneers ruin your teeth"](/blog/do-veneers-ruin-your-teeth) stories are a different procedure from a 0.3 mm veneer, even though both are sold under the same name.

A warranty is not a claim that nothing will happen. It is a statement about who pays if something does. Ours covers the veneer for five years, in writing, handed to you at Visit 3 on the day your veneers are bonded. Normal care, routine cleanings and a night guard if you grind are expected. Since most early problems with veneers show up in the first two years, a five-year term covers that window with margin to spare, which is the sensible way to think about a restoration that is designed to be replaced rather than to last forever. [What a veneer warranty covers](/blog/veneer-warranty-what-it-covers) has the terms other Miami practices publish for comparison.

The warranty is affordable for us because our ceramist works in the building, so a remake is a few hours of lab time rather than an outside invoice. That same lab is what makes replacement in year twelve or fifteen a short visit rather than a new project: the design file, the shade records and the people who made the first set are still here.

sections.h2: The better question to ask yourself

blocks.p: If you want to keep the option of untouched natural teeth, veneers are not the right tool, and bonding or Invisalign may be. If what you want is a smile you can rely on, with the understanding that it will be maintained like anything else you use every day, veneers are a well-studied way to get it. [Who is a candidate for veneers](/blog/who-is-a-candidate-for-veneers) covers the health side of that decision, and [how to take care of porcelain veneers](/blog/how-to-take-care-of-porcelain-veneers) covers the daily side.

A single veneer at Xiluet Smiles is $1,000 and the 20-veneer [Smile Design](/smile-design-miami) package is $5,999, both with the written warranty; the [cost page](/veneers-cost-miami) lists everything else. If you would like to know, tooth by tooth, how much preparation your own teeth would need, send three photos through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation). The written estimate says veneer or crown for each tooth before you pay a deposit, and that estimate is the real answer to how reversible your particular case would be.

faq.a: Yes, by a dentist. The porcelain is cut through with a fine bur, lifted off and the bonding resin is polished from the enamel, with the area numbed for comfort. The tooth underneath is intact but slightly matte where it was prepared, so it is covered again the same visit with a new veneer or, if far more enamel was removed elsewhere, a crown.

No. Even a 0.3 mm preparation removes enamel that does not grow back, and no-prep veneers still have to be drilled off and the resin cleaned away. The accurate word is enamel-preserving: a thin preparation keeps the nerve untouched and leaves enough enamel for future veneers to bond to, but the tooth will always need a restoration from then on.

faq.q: How long do veneers last before they need replacing?
faq.a: Typically 10 to 15 years, often longer. Pooled data on more than 6,500 veneers found 95.5% still in place at 10 years, and one 20-year study found 91%. Our longevity article goes through the numbers; the short version is that a veneer reaching the end of its life is replaced on the same tooth.

faq.q: What do teeth look like after veneers are removed?
faq.a: Like your own teeth with a slightly matte front surface where 0.3 mm was prepared. They are more sensitive to cold and stain faster than untouched enamel, and after years under a veneer they no longer match their neighbors, which is why removal and replacement happen in the same appointment.

faq.q: Will I need a crown when my veneers are replaced?
faq.a: Usually not, if the first veneers were conservative. A 0.3 mm preparation leaves about 0.7 mm of enamel for the next veneer to bond to. Crowns become likely when a previous dentist removed 0.7 mm or more and reached dentin, which is one reason to ask any clinic how much enamel it plans to take.

faq.q: Does the 5-year warranty mean the veneers will not fail?
faq.a: No. It means that if a veneer chips, cracks or comes loose under normal use within five years, we repair or replace it at no charge. It is handed to you in writing at Visit 3. Normal care, regular cleanings and a night guard if you grind are expected.
